$comment: Shared contract between the two integrity classifiers: optimind-journal/scripts/optimind_core.py (gates the nightly Reflection, drives the Hermes plugin) and dashboard/src/lib/status.ts (runs in the browser with no backend). Both must produce identical statuses, so both test against THIS file. All data here is synthetic -- never copy real journal content into this public repo. Journal text uses the real structural shapes observed in production: bracketed text inside User entries, protocol mirror lines, qualifiers in parentheses, and incomplete lines that state a fact without the value the schema requires.

cases.name: matched day
cases.why: Both records agree. The baseline everything else is measured against.

cases.name: journal only - the write defect
cases.why: The user supplied the data and the structured write lost it. This must never be reported as a behavior miss.

cases.name: structured only - the audit log is incomplete
cases.why: The inverse defect: numbers exist that the append-only log never recorded.

cases.name: mixed - divergence both ways
cases.why: Each record holds something the other lacks.

cases.name: current day is never a miss
cases.why: A day still being lived has not failed to record anything yet.

cases.name: blackout - no turn occurred
cases.why: Nothing was captured because nothing happened. Distinct from a lost write.

cases.name: no_data - turns happened but produced no fact
cases.why: A capture-ritual problem, not a blackout and not a write defect.
cases.journal:
### 09:00 | User
how should I plan tomorrow?

cases.name: needs_input - the journal line is incomplete
cases.why: A meal with no time cannot be projected into JSON at all. No rerun fixes it, so it must not sit in the integrity gate forever.

cases.name: needs_input alongside a real defect
cases.why: One repairable field plus one unrepairable. The repairable one must still fail the gate.

cases.name: arrays compare by count
cases.why: A meal has no stable identity, so three mirror lines against one entry means two facts were lost.

cases.name: partially resolvable array splits the deficit
cases.why: Two mirrored coffees, one missing its dose: one repairable, one needs the user.
cases.journal:
### 22:00 | Dashboard
[caffeine] 09:05 espresso, ~65mg (est.)
[caffeine] 09:10 black coffee, caffeine amount not stated

cases.name: bracketed text in User entries is not a fact
cases.why: Users paste photo captions and timestamps. A file-wide bracket scan would invent divergence.
cases.journal:
### 09:38 | User
[attached cafe menu photo] what should i get
[2:31 PM] pasted timestamp

### 09:40 | Dashboard
[sleep.quality] 3/5

cases.name: protocol mirror lines are planning, not capture
cases.why: Counting these would report permanent unfixable divergence on every day with a protocol.

cases.name: not_reported is not a skip
cases.why: Nobody asked. Recording it as a skipped habit is the miscount this whole model exists to stop.

cases.name: missing files do not crash
cases.why: Days with neither record are common at the edges of a range.

cases.name: one mirror line can carry several entries
cases.why: The writer batches a whole category onto one line. Counting lines instead of entries reported real, matching data as lost writes.

cases.name: a semicolon inside parentheses does not split an entry
cases.why: `15:00 60mg matcha (native L-theanine; AFTER 14:00 cutoff)` is one drink, not two.
cases.journal:
### 22:00 | Dashboard
[caffeine] 15:00 60mg matcha lemonade (native L-theanine; AFTER 14:00 cutoff)

cases.name: a time range is one entry, not two
cases.why: `18:30-19:30 walk` would count as two if we counted bare timestamps.

cases.name: a batched line still detects a genuine shortfall
cases.why: Splitting must not become a way to hide real loss: three mirrored meals against one stored entry is still two lost.

cases.name: narrative [event] lines are context, not captured metrics
cases.why: The writer records real-world events -- an interview, a post going out -- through the same block. They have no place in the structured log, so counting them reports a divergence nothing can ever fix.
cases.journal:
### 22:00 | Dashboard
[sleep.quality] 3/5
[event] interviews 14:25-17:00 completed
[tomorrow.priority] follow up with the recruiter
